methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective clinicopathological study of 106 gastric cancer patients who underwent curative R0 resection without neoadjuvant therapy. Immunohistochemistry for CD163+ (M2 TAMs) and CD34 (MVD) at invasive front with quantification by two independent pathologists. Statistical methods include Mann-Whitney U test, Pearson correlation, Kaplan-Meier analysis, Cox regression. Median follow-up 61-69 months adequate. However, retrospective design, single-center, small sample size (44 deaths), and use of median as cutoff (no a priori cutoff) are methodological limitations.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Retrospective analysis of clinicopathological correlates (M2 TAMs, MVD) and survival outcomes. Direct clinical relevance: MVD identified as independent prognostic factor (HR 0.97, p=0.03) associated with improved survival. However, M2 TAMs alone not prognostic. LoE is 3b (case-control/retrospective cohort). Findings suggest prognostic role at invasive front but require prospective validation.

reporting_quality.justification: Excellent STROBE adherence: clear study population definition, detailed immunohistochemistry protocols (antibody clones, staining methods), blinded pathological assessment, well-reported statistical methods including assumption testing (Schoenfeld residuals). However, data availability limited: no mention of depositing tissue samples or imaging files; institutional pathological data not publicly shared.

novelty_literature.justification: M2 TAM infiltration at gastric cancer invasive front is known to correlate with poor outcomes. Prior meta-analyses and regional studies (Park et al., Wu et al., Yin et al.) have established these associations. Current contribution is confirmatory analysis in a Polish cohort showing MVD (not M2 TAMs) as independent prognostic factor—an incremental regional finding rather than novel discovery.

writing_presentation.justification: Clear, well-organized manuscript with detailed introduction contextualizing the study within prior literature. Methods precisely describe histopathology and statistics. Results presented in tables and Kaplan-Meier curves. Discussion appropriately places findings in context of conflicting prior results on M2 TAM prognostic significance. Authors acknowledge limitations candidly.

key_strengths: Focused analysis on invasive front, a biologically distinct region where M2 TAMs and MVD may have different prognostic significance than other tumor regions
Independent blinded pathological assessment by two experienced pathologists with standardized quantification
Long median follow-up (61-69 months) with all deaths cancer-related, providing robust survival data
Multivariate Cox regression adjusting for established prognostic factors (pT, pN)
key_concerns: Retrospective single-center design limits generalizability; no prospective external validation
Small sample size (n=106, 44 deaths) with wide confidence intervals; limited statistical power for detecting associations
Use of median as cutoff rather than a priori biologically justified threshold; risk of overfitting
Restriction to R0 resection without neoadjuvant therapy may not reflect modern practice
Unexpected finding (higher MVD associated with improved survival) contradicts prior meta-analysis; mechanism unclear
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a competent retrospective clinicopathological study that extends prior work to a European population and reveals MVD as an unexpected favorable prognostic marker at the invasive front. The well-designed immunohistochemistry and survival analysis justify tier 3. However, single-center design, small sample, and lack of independent validation limit higher placement. Minor revisions should clarify the unexpected MVD finding and acknowledge that conclusions apply to selected R0-resected patients only.
